subject: SIG: encryption section — KMS/HSM and rotation window clarification
messages:
From: Elena Torres <elena.torres@acmehealth.com>
To: markus.klein@redwood.com
Cc: sig@acmehealth.com
Date: 2029-08-11T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: SIG: encryption section — rotation windows & HSM details

Hi Markus,

Thanks for taking SIG for Acme Health. We're working through the encryption section and had a couple of items we can't fully answer from the questionnaire alone:

- Do you use HSM-backed key storage for customer keys in your Hosted offering, or are keys always cloud-KMS-managed? If HSM is used, who is the provider and are keys non-exportable?
- What's your default key rotation cadence and is there an overlap/grace period between old/new keys to avoid token/secret failures? Please specify the rotation window (days) and whether rotation is automatic or manual.
- For at-rest encryption, what algorithms and key sizes are used? For in-transit, which TLS versions and cipher suites are supported?
- Can you provide an example rotation audit (redacted) showing a prior rotation and the associated timestamps/logs?

If you can attach short artifacts (diagram of key flow, a sample rotation log CSV, and the completed SIG PDF for the encryption section) that will speed review. If certain items are only available under an NDA or a secure upload, let me know and we can arrange.

Best,
Elena
Information Security Manager, Acme Health

---
Note: Acme requires vendor answers for SIG v2.1; we expect the encryption section to be thorough as it will drive our vendor risk decision.
From: markus.klein@redwood.com
To: Elena Torres <elena.torres@acmehealth.com>
Cc: monica.patel@redwood.com, mina.haddad@redwood.com
Date: 2029-08-11T13:48:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SIG: encryption section — rotation windows & HSM details

Hi Elena — thanks for the clear questions. Attached are concise answers and three small artifacts: redwood_encryption_answers_SIG_v1.pdf (completed encryption section), kms-hsm-architecture-diagram.pdf, and a redacted rotation_audit_sample.csv. Quick highlights below; the PDF contains the SIG formatted responses.

- HSM vs KMS: Our Hosted and Dedicated offerings use cloud KMS (AWS KMS / Azure Key Vault) for key management; for Hosted we operate customer keys in KMS with HSM-backed root keys provided by the cloud vendor (non-exportable). For Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem) customers we support integration with customer-managed HSMs (PKCS#11) and can accept keys that never leave the HSM.

- Exportability: Customer keys in cloud KMS are non-exportable. For Private/HSM integrations exportability depends on customer configuration — we recommend keys remain non-exportable in HSM.

- Rotation cadence & overlap: Default automated rotation for system-managed keys is 365 days. We support manual and customer-triggered rotations for customer-managed keys. We maintain a configurable overlap window of 30 days where both old and new keys are accepted for decryption to avoid token expiry issues; write operations use the new key after rotation. The overlap can be shortened to 7 days for tight-security customers, or extended for migration reasons.

- Algorithms: At-rest data is encrypted with AES-256-GCM (data keys) with envelope encryption using KMS-managed keys (RSA/EC for signing where applicable). In-transit uses TLS 1.2+ (we strongly recommend TLS 1.3) and we support modern cipher suites (AEAD ciphers, forward secrecy).

- Audit/logs: Rotation events and key usage are logged to our audit pipeline (immutable event stream forwarded to customer SIEM for Dedicated/Private or retained in our audit store for Hosted with configurable export). I've attached a small redacted CSV showing a rotation event with timestamps, actor id, and key id. If you need a signed attestation from our cloud HSM provider, we can obtain their standard supplier attestation (vendor-dependent).

Next steps: if Acme needs full logs or vendor attestation we can either: 1) upload artifacts to your secure portal (send upload link), or 2) execute a simple NDA and place files in a shared drive. Which do you prefer? Happy to hop on a 20-minute call to walk through the diagram.

Thanks,
Markus Klein
Head of Security & Compliance — Redwood Inference

Attachments (3): redwood_encryption_answers_SIG_v1.pdf (16KB stub), kms-hsm-architecture-diagram.pdf (48KB stub), rotation_audit_sample.csv (2KB stub)

Hi Markus — thanks for the quick turnaround and the attachments, those are helpful. A couple of follow-ups after reviewing the PDF and diagram:

1) The PDF states a configurable overlap of 30 days with an option for 7 days for "tight-security customers". For our procurement risk profile we need to lock that to a maximum overlap of 7 days. Is that a policy you can enforce per-account, or does it require engineering changes?

2) The sample CSV is sufficient to understand format, but we need a machine-verifiable log export for one prior rotation (redacted key ids OK) that includes: rotation_start_ts, rotation_complete_ts, actor (service/account), and a signature or checksum. Can you indicate how quickly you can produce that?

3) Finally, for HSM provider attestation: we need a statement from the HSM vendor confirming non-exportability and FIPS 140-2/3 status (if applicable). If the vendor attestation is not provided directly, would Redwood be able to provide a documented vendor-signed attestation or a copy of the cloud provider's key custody whitepaper?

We can do a 20-minute call tomorrow morning (09:00–11:00 PT) if that helps. Pasting a few preferred slots below.

Slots: 2029-08-13 09:30 PT, 2029-08-13 10:30 PT, 2029-08-13 11:00 PT

Thanks — Elena

Elena — thanks for the clarifying questions. Answers inline: 

1) Enforcing a 7-day maximum overlap: Yes — we can enforce a per-account policy. For Hosted accounts this is a configuration toggle we can apply within the tenant control plane; no code change required. For Dedicated/Private customers we'll coordinate with infra to update the customer config and will confirm via change record. We'll note this as a required security control in the SIG response if Acme elects the 7-day policy.

2) Machine-verifiable rotation export: We can produce a redacted export within 3 business days. Our export includes rotation_start_ts, rotation_complete_ts, actor_id, key_id (redacted), and an HMAC checksum over the CSV lines signed by our audit signing key. For Hosted customers we can also provide the cloud KMS audit event IDs (e.g., CloudTrail event ids) for cross-validation. Please confirm the preferred delivery method (secure portal upload vs NDA + shared drive).

3) HSM attestation: For cloud KMS we can provide the cloud provider's key custody documentation and their FIPS attestation links. If Acme requires a signed vendor attestation naming Redwood specifically we can request the vendor-stamped statement (this may take 5–10 business days depending on vendor). We can start with the provider whitepapers immediately.

Call: 2029-08-13 09:30 PT works for me; booking a 20-minute slot now unless you prefer a different one.

Next actions:
- I'll flag the tenant config change path with our platform team and provide an internal ticket by EOD.
- If you confirm delivery method, I will schedule the redacted export and vendor attestation request.

Regards,
Markus
